name: Urumi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Tupian known from wordlists; Glottolog cites only classification work (Eriksen & Galucio 2014)

sources.citation: Gabas Jr., Nilson. 1999. A grammar of Karo, Tupí (Brazil). PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 246 pp.
sources.note: Describes KARO, not Urumi. §1.1 (p. 1): Karo classified with 'three other languages, Ramarama, Uruku and Urumi, given as extinct (Rodrigues 1964)', but 'the different languages considered its sisters might be, in fact, Karo itself, which was labeled differently by different researchers'. §2.5 Stress (pp. 30-33): 'Stress occurs basically on the last syllable of Karo words. Less frequently, it occurs on penultimate syllables. These occurrences are predictable in terms of segmental and suprasegmental factors.' (a voiced-stop onset /b, r, g/ of the last syllable shifts stress to the penult; nasal…

sources.citation: Gabas Jr., Nilson. 1989. Estudo fonológico da língua Karo (Arara de Rondônia). MA thesis, Universidade Estadual de Campinas (supervisor Aryon Rodrigues).
sources.note: Full phonology of Karo, the language Gabas (2000) identifies with the Urumi wordlists; would give the earliest stress description for the Karo/Urumi complex. Relevant only if the catalog accepts the Urumi = Karo identity.
sources.venue: MA thesis, Universidade Estadual de Campinas (supervisor Aryon Rodrigues)

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1932. Wortlisten aus Amazonien. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 24: 93-119.
sources.note: Cited by Lévi-Strauss 1950 (fn. 3) as a second Nimuendajú source on the Ntogapid/Rama-rama group; may contain accent-marked Ramarama-branch words but almost certainly no Urumi data or stress statement.
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Américanistes

sources.citation: Gabas Jr., Nilson. 2000. Genetic relationship within the Ramaráma family of the Tupi stock (Brazil). In Hein van der Voort & Simon van de Kerke (eds.), Indigenous languages of lowland South America (Indigenous Languages of Latin America 1), 71-82. Leiden: CNWS.
sources.note: Compares the seven published Ramarama wordlists with Karo. §8 (pp. 78-79): Lévi-Strauss's 145-word Urumí list, 85.5% correspond to Karo words; §9 (p. 79): Rondon's 105-word Urumí list, 55.2% correspond, 'Rondon only exceptionally uses special symbols in his transcription of Urumí, and his orthographic conventions are based on Portuguese spelling'. §10 (p. 79): the wordlist languages 'are, in fact, the same language (or at least dialects of the same language), Karo.' Nothing on stress.
sources.venue: Indigenous languages of lowland South America (Indigenous Languages of Latin America 1)

sources.citation: Lévi-Strauss, Claude. 1950. Documents Rama-Rama. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 39: 73-84. (150-word Urumi list collected 28 Nov 1938 at the seringal de Piratini, rio Gi-Paraná; 'Observations sur le système phonologique' pp. 74-76; 'Observations sur la structure des mots' pp. 76-77; vocabulary pp. 78-84.)
sources.note: The phonology section discusses only the vowel system (5 oral + 5 nasal vowels, a possible schwa and a velar vowel), vowel-sequence restrictions, two semivowels and the consonant inventory by position; nothing on accent, stress or syllable prominence. His transcriptions carry acute accents on some vowels (iéiú 'eau', karó 'arara', ma-ikúp 'perle') but the accent mark is not explained anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent the whole volume scanned for accent/tonique/syllabe finds nothing in the article).
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Américanistes

sources.citation: Rondon, Cândido M. S. & João Barbosa de Faria. 1948. Glossário geral das tribos silvícolas de Mato-Grosso e outras da Amazônia e do Norte do Brasil, Tomo I. Comissão Rondon, Publicação n. 76, Anexo 5. Rio de Janeiro: Imprensa Nacional. 257 pp. 'Vocabulário dos índios Urumi, colhido pelo então Cel. Rondon' pp. 213-216 (105 words, collected April 1913).
sources.note: Wordlist only; no grammatical or phonological description of Urumi. The book-wide 'Convenções adotadas' item IV (p. 11) says the accents written on vowels 'corresponde[m] aos sons fortes e longos de sílabas tônicas' (mark the strong, long sounds of stressed syllables); the Urumi entries carry such marks on individual words (e.g. Inacá 'cabeça', Gikiêgá 'calcanhar', Mopáope 'balaio', Uôreôchi 'abano'), both word-final and non-final (rough scanned count: ~48 of 77 parsed entries accented, ~26 on the last vowel). No rule stated.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1925. As tribus do alto Madeira. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 17: 137-172.
sources.note: scanned text of the volume only. Urumi mentioned once (p. 145): from photographs 'parece-me possivel um parentesco della [the Ntogapid] com os Urumi do Rio Tarumá'; gives a Ntogapid/Rama-rama word comparison, no Urumi data, nothing on stress.
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Américanistes

sources.note: Cites only Rondon & Faria 1948 (numerals table); says extinct after 1913; no phonology.
